questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: One important part of the registration process was the health insurance documentation. Even though I had the European Health Insurance Card, it still had to be approved by a German health insurance provider. After this, the provider sent the confirmation directly to the university. This was a necessary administrative step before the enrolment could be completed, so it is something future students should be aware of in advance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office in Heidelberg was very helpful whenever I needed assistance. They did not respond very often by phone, but they were reliable in replying to emails, so email was the best way to get support.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful in registering for the courses I wanted. At my host institution, it was generally not necessary to register for the classes themselves, but only for the exams. This made the process much easier and gave me flexibility in choosing and attending courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Take the process as it comes and try not to stress too much, even if it feels bureaucratic at times. In the end, things usually work out.

My advice would be to stay patient and not worry too much if the process seems slow or administrative. It can feel complicated at first, but it becomes clearer step by step.

It is a good idea to be patient and prepared for some bureaucracy. Even if the process takes time, it is manageable, and the International Office can help if needed.

Do not panic if the registration process feels confusing in the beginning. It involves several administrative steps, but if you follow the instructions carefully, it will work out.

Be prepared for a process that can feel quite bureaucratic, and make sure to complete each step carefully. It is also helpful to communicate by email, since that was the most reliable way to get assistance.

Try to stay organized and keep track of deadlines and required documents. The process can take time, but it is easier if you approach it calmly and one step at a time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust to the local culture, as life in Germany felt quite similar to life in Denmark in many ways. Because of these similarities, it was easy to settle in quickly and adapt to everyday life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found that the culture was somewhat more strict than what I was used to in Denmark, especially in relation to rules, structure, and formal procedures. However, since Germany and Denmark are quite similar in many ways, this was not a major challenge and was easy to adjust to over time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated that the culture felt more formal, as it created a sense of structure, respect, and seriousness in both academic and everyday settings. At the same time, it was still easy to adapt because German and Danish culture are similar in many ways.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: ry to learn some German before or during your stay, join Erasmus events to build a social network, and do not stress too much about the practical and administrative parts of the exchange, as things usually work out in the end.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to always carry some cash with you, since not all places accept card payments. This is especially useful in everyday situations such as smaller shops, cafés, or local restaurants.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was improving my German. It was valuable to be able to practice the language in everyday life and to feel more confident using it over the course of the semester.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was being away from home and adjusting to living independently in a different country. Even though it became easier over time, this was probably the most difficult part of the experience for me.
